Title: Celebrating Midwives on the International Day of the Midwife
NewsSummary: Dean's message to midwives during the International Day of the Midwife
NewsContent:
A Message from Dr Eunice Ndirangu, Dean at AKU-SONAM in East Africa during the International Day of the Midwife

As we celebrate the International Day of the Midwife, I would like to acknowledge all the midwives working at the frontline during this challenging time. Pregnancy, childbearing and delivery are normal functions that cannot be postponed or delayed because of a pandemic. The pandemic may have stopped a lot of activity around the world, but women will continue to get pregnant, require antenatal care and continue to give birth. This is why midwives are so important: because their work goes on regardless of prevailing circumstances. Midwives continue to provide communities, health facilities and families with sexual and reproductive health services, maternal and child health services as well as any other general healthcare services because they often serve as nurses too. Therefore, it is important to stand in solidarity with midwives as we celebrate their contribution to health systems all over the world.

The WHO declared 2020 as the “Year of the Nurse and Midwife" which means that throughout this year, we will celebrate the contributions of nurses and midwives to our health systems, economies and families. The theme for this year is “Midwives with women: celebrate, demonstrate, mobilise, unite", which emphasizes the importance of midwives and women standing in solidarity with each other. As AKU, we celebrate midwives who continue to provide reproductive education to teenagers remotely; we celebrate midwives who enable safe deliveries amid curfews and quarantines and we celebrate midwives all over the world who work tirelessly to strengthen family units and bring life into the world. As women, we stand with you and recognise that our children would not be safe without your contribution and neither would our families. May you enjoy this day with your colleagues, families, patients and associations as you observe the various government directives and remember that we stand with you as you stand with women and children all over the world!
